Origin-destination costs

Source: R/acc.R
acc_cost_matrix.Rd

Builds the long table of travel costs between origins (such as tract centroids from acc_centroids()) and sites (such as library outlets), either as straight-line distance or from a table you supply, such as tract-to-tract travel times from OpenTimes (https://opentimes.org).

Usage

acc_cost_matrix(
  from,
  to,
  from_id,
  to_id,
  method = c("euclidean", "provided"),
  cost = NULL,
  max_cost = NULL
)

Arguments

from, to

Origins and destinations: data frames or sf objects with one row per unit. For method = "euclidean" both must be sf points in the same projected CRS.

from_id, to_id

<tidy-select> One column each of unique, non-missing IDs.

method

"euclidean" for straight-line distance in the units of the CRS (meters for EPSG:3310), or "provided" to validate and filter the table passed as cost.

cost

For method = "provided", a data frame with columns from, to and cost. Rename the columns of a travel-time table to these first. Must be NULL for method = "euclidean".

max_cost

Optional positive number. Pairs costing more are dropped, which keeps the table small. Set it to at least the catchment you will pass to acc_e2sfca().

Value

A tibble with columns from, to and cost, sorted by origin and then destination in the order of from and to.

Details

Euclidean costs are computed in blocks of origins, about five million distances at a time, so the full origin-by-site matrix is never held in memory. The returned table still has one row per pair, so set max_cost to keep it small in a large run.

For a provided table, acc_cost_matrix() checks the three columns, rejects missing or negative costs and repeated origin-destination pairs, and drops rows whose IDs are not in from or to, with a message counting them (a national travel-time file covers far more tracts than one state). If no row matches, the IDs probably differ in type or format, such as numeric GEOIDs that have lost a leading zero, and the function stops. A pair missing from the table counts as out of reach.

See also

acc_e2sfca().

Examples

origins <- sf::st_as_sf(
  data.frame(id = c("a", "b", "c"), x = c(0, 3, 6), y = c(0, 4, 8)),
  coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 3310
)
sites <- sf::st_as_sf(
  data.frame(site = c("x", "y"), x = c(0, 6), y = c(0, 0)),
  coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 3310
)
acc_cost_matrix(origins, sites, id, site)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   from  to     cost
#>   <chr> <chr> <dbl>
#> 1 a     x         0
#> 2 a     y         6
#> 3 b     x         5
#> 4 b     y         5
#> 5 c     x        10
#> 6 c     y         8
acc_cost_matrix(origins, sites, id, site, max_cost = 6)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   from  to     cost
#>   <chr> <chr> <dbl>
#> 1 a     x         0
#> 2 a     y         6
#> 3 b     x         5
#> 4 b     y         5

# A provided table, such as travel times in minutes.
times <- data.frame(from = c("a", "b", "z"), to = c("x", "y", "x"),
                    cost = c(5, 12, 3))
acc_cost_matrix(origins, sites, id, site, method = "provided", cost = times)
#> Dropped 1 row of `cost` whose origin or destination is not in `from` or `to`.
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   from  to     cost
#>   <chr> <chr> <dbl>
#> 1 a     x         5
#> 2 b     y        12
